split.title: Computer-on time
split.afk_note: AFK is time when the computer was on but you did not touch the keyboard or mouse for {minutes} or longer. Time when the computer was off or asleep is not included at all — ActivityWatch records nothing then.
split.other_note: Other at the computer means you were active but the time did not land in any application: switching desktops, untitled windows and filtered-out system processes ({system}).
split.lenient_note: Active in the {where} {listed} also includes AFK time while their window is focused: on a call or watching a video you listen without pressing anything. At most {cap} is credited from each AFK stretch — {counted} over the period, and it no longer counts as AFK.

categories.title: Categories
categories.uncategorized_note: {label} — {apps}, {duration}. Assign them to categories in {file}; sorted by time, descending.

days.title: Activity over the last {days}
days.none: No activity recorded in the last {days}.
days.aria: Activity per day over the last {days}

by_month.title: By month
by_month.gaps: No data — {days}: {list}. The computer was off: these days are left out of “d” and the daily average, and count as inactive in the banner.

heat.title: When you are active
heat.densest: densest: {duration} (sum over all weeks of the period)

focus.title: Attention fragmentation
focus.caption: By category: share of time in blocks over {duration} and the average block
focus.note_block: A block is a continuous stay in one application. Focus shorter than {dwell} (alt-tab, a taskbar click, a notification) does not break the block and is not counted as a switch: its seconds go to the ongoing block.
focus.note_pause: A pause longer than {gap} closes the block without a switch: coming back to a different application after a break is a fresh start, not a jump of attention.
focus.note_deep: Focused is the share of active time in blocks longer than {duration}. Hover a category to see its switches per hour.

rhythm.title: Daily rhythm
rhythm.after_title: {duration} of active time after midnight, {days} with such activity
rhythm.caption: By week, starting Monday: usual start and end of the day
rhythm.note_day: A day runs from {start} to {start} the next day: a session that ended at 02:33 is the end of the previous day, not the start of a new one.
rhythm.note_bounds: Start and end are the first and last active moment of the day; “usual” is the median over days with activity. The first observed day has no start and today has no end: there the boundary comes from the data, not from your schedule.
rhythm.note_after: After midnight is active time from 00:00 to {start} and its share of all active time.

games.title: Games
games.none: No processes from the {category} category were seen.
games.order: Sorted by last launch. A game session breaks after a pause over {duration}.
games.unplayed: Installed but not launched during the observed period ({n})

warn.no_afk: No aw-watcher-afk bucket found — time is counted without the away filter, so numbers are inflated.
warn.created: Created {file} from the starter set — edit that file from now on.
warn.demo: Demo mode: the data is made up and is not anyone's real activity.

footer.sessions: A session breaks on a pause over {duration} or on being away from the computer. Percentages in categories and the top list are of active time.
footer.design: Design — Material Design 2: 2014 palettes, elevation levels 2/6/12/24dp.

category_warnings.unreadable: {file} cannot be read ({error}) — using the starter set.
category_warnings.empty: {file} is empty — using the starter set.
category_warnings.unknown_policy: unknown AFK policy “{policy}” in “{category}” — treating it as “{fallback}”
category_warnings.duplicate_process: process “{process}” is listed in both “{first}” and “{second}” — keeping “{first}”
category_warnings.duplicate_pattern: pattern “{pattern}” is listed in both “{first}” and “{second}” — keeping “{first}”
category_warnings.pattern_conflict: “{process}” matches patterns of several categories ({detail}) — using “{winner}”

font_warnings.missing_face: {stem}.woff2/.woff/.ttf not found in {directory} — weight {weight} falls back to the system font.
font_warnings.none_embedded: no font file was embedded — the report uses the system font.
